Tombstone Arizona Day Trip: Your Complete Wild West Adventure Guide

"The Town Too Tough to Die" lives up to its name. Tombstone, Arizona — site of the famous Gunfight at the O.K. Corral — offers visitors a genuine step back into the Wild West. Silver mining built it, outlaws made it famous, and today it's one of Arizona's most entertaining day trip destinations.

The short answer: Tombstone is a long run each way down I-10 and AZ-80, so plan a 12- to 14-hour day. Twelve hours earns two free hours, so you pay for 10: $1,250 before tax on the Luxury SUV (6 seats, $125/hr), or $1,450 on the Executive Sprinter (14 seats, $145/hr) — about $104 per person with a full van. Book it as our Tombstone and Bisbee tour.

Tombstone Basics

Location & Access

  • Distance from Phoenix: 180 miles southeast
  • Route: I-10 and AZ-80
  • Nearest Major City: Tucson (70 miles north)
  • Elevation: 4,539 feet

The History

Tombstone's story is American legend:

  • 1877: Ed Schieffelin discovers silver
  • 1879: Town founded, named Tombstone
  • 1881: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral (October 26)
  • 1882: Wyatt Earp's Vendetta Ride
  • 1886: Mines flood, decline begins
  • Later designated a National Historic Landmark
  • Today: Living-history tourist destination

The Experience

Tombstone is essentially a living museum:

  • Authentic 1880s buildings
  • Costumed characters everywhere
  • Daily gunfight reenactments
  • Saloons, shops, and restaurants
  • Very tourist-friendly, slightly campy, genuinely fun

The Journey to Tombstone

The Route

  • Phoenix to Tucson: I-10 East (110 miles)
  • Tucson to Tombstone: AZ-80 via Benson (70 miles)
  • Total: 180 miles

Along the Way

Optional stops on the route:

  • Picacho Peak: Site of the Civil War's westernmost battle
  • Tucson: Lunch stop, stretch break
  • Benson: Gateway to Kartchner Caverns

Why Not Drive Yourself?

  • The round-trip driving is tiring
  • The route through the desert is monotonous
  • Saloons are more fun without designated-driver concerns
  • Arrive rested, ready to explore

What to Do in Tombstone

Must-See Attractions

O.K. Corral

  • Site of the famous 1881 gunfight
  • Reenactments daily (check schedules)
  • Museum and exhibits
  • Photography opportunities

Tombstone Courthouse State Historic Park

  • Restored 1882 courthouse
  • Excellent museum
  • Gallows in the courtyard
  • Historical exhibits

Bird Cage Theatre

  • 1881 variety hall and saloon
  • Original furnishings
  • Bullet holes still in the walls
  • Allegedly haunted

Boot Hill Graveyard

  • Final resting place of gunfight victims
  • Colorful epitaphs
  • Historic atmosphere
  • Free admission

Gunfight Reenactments

Multiple daily shows:

  • O.K. Corral: Most famous, theatrical
  • Helldorado Town: Alternative shows
  • Street performances: Random encounters throughout the day

Check schedules — shows typically run in the afternoon and near sunset.

Saloons & Dining

VenueTypeKnown For
Allen Street saloonsSaloon/RestaurantHistoric atmosphere, burgers
Restored Victorian roomsSaloonVictorian elegance
Main Street family diningFamily diningWestern comfort food

Shopping

Allen Street Offerings:

  • Western wear and boots
  • Silver jewelry
  • Native American crafts
  • Old West memorabilia
  • Toy guns and costumes (kids love it)

Ghost Tours

Several operators offer evening tours:

  • Tombstone Ghost Tour
  • Walking tours of haunted locations
  • Best experienced in the off-season for atmosphere

Nearby Addition: Bisbee

Just 25 miles from Tombstone, Bisbee offers a completely different vibe:

  • Historic copper mining town
  • Artsy, bohemian atmosphere
  • Unique architecture
  • Great restaurants and galleries
  • Queen Mine Tour (underground mine experience)

Many visitors combine both towns for a full Southern Arizona experience — that's exactly what our Tombstone and Bisbee tour is built around.

Seasonal Considerations

Spring (March-May)

  • Weather: Perfect (70s-80s)
  • Crowds: Moderate
  • Events: Wyatt Earp Days (Memorial Day weekend)

Summer (June-August)

  • Weather: Hot but not Phoenix-hot (90s)
  • Crowds: Lighter (too hot for some)
  • Tip: Start early, take a midday break

Fall (September-November)

  • Weather: Ideal (70s-80s)
  • Crowds: Heavy for Helldorado Days (October)
  • Events: Helldorado (third weekend in October)

Winter (December-February)

  • Weather: Cool (50s-60s)
  • Crowds: Light
  • Charm: Quiet, atmospheric

Tombstone Day Trip FAQ

Q: Is Tombstone "touristy"?
A: Yes, unapologetically so. Embrace it — it's entertaining.

Q: How long do I need in Tombstone?
A: 4-6 hours covers the highlights thoroughly.

Q: Is it worth combining with Bisbee?
A: If you have time, absolutely. They're complementary experiences, and a 15+ hour day earns three free hours.

Q: Are there gunfights all day?
A: Multiple daily shows, typically afternoon and evening.

Q: Can we drink in the saloons?
A: Yes — they're real, functioning bars with great atmosphere. And nobody in your group has to drive home.

Q: Is Tombstone good for kids?
A: Excellent for families — kids love the costumes, gunfights, and Western atmosphere.
